value.overview: The Olive Warbler (Peucedramus taeniatus) is a warbler recorded in the United States. Field recognition often comes from olive-gray body, orange-brown head in adults, white wing patches, and deliberate movement in pine or oak-pine trees. In the U.S. source data, it appeared in 2 state or DC summaries, including AZ, NM. It is most associated with Forests:  Mesoamerican Highland and Forests:  Mesoamerican Pine-Oak, and local season should be checked before trip planning.
value.classification: The Olive Warbler belongs to the family New World Warblers in the order Passeriformes. This is the practical birding classification used for the BirdIntel profile cache.
value.identification: Look for olive-gray body, orange-brown head in adults, white wing patches, and deliberate movement in pine or oak-pine trees. Also use size, posture, flight style, voice, behavior, habitat, and season. Plumage can vary by sex, age, molt, and light, so the safest identification comes from combining several field marks rather than relying on one color or feature.
